summary: The bill amends 5 U.S.C. 8462 to apply the same annual price-index-based COLA formula (rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent) used for CSRS annuities to FERS annuities, effective for all adjustments made after enactment and for annuities already in payment.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends 5 U.S.C. § 8462 to provide FERS annuities with the same full CPI-based COLA that CSRS annuities receive. Because FERS covers the large majority of current federal retirees, this change directly increases mandatory federal outlays for retirement benefits on an ongoing basis. The legislation therefore expands government spending.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection. It addresses only the indexing formula for existing federal retirement annuities.
No provisions address health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, or the structure of the health-care delivery system.
The bill does not mention firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, visa, asylum, or border-enforcement provisions appear in the text.
The legislation is silent on reproductive health services or abortion access.
While some federal annuitants are former DoD civilians, the bill makes a uniform, government-wide change to FERS COLAs and does not alter military pay, troop levels, or defense appropriations.
No environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions are present.
Federal retirement annuities are earned pension benefits rather than means-tested welfare programs such as SNAP or TANF; the bill does not modify eligibility or funding for those programs.
The bill does not address schools, student aid, or education funding formulas.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement appear.
The legislation contains no sentencing, policing, or corrections provisions.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are addressed.

By increasing mandatory spending, the bill will widen future deficits, but it does not articulate a fiscal policy stance on debt reduction versus investment; the primary purpose is COLA parity, not debt management.
The bill does not create, expand, or limit protections on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
No foreign-assistance authorizations or appropriations are involved.
The legislation is unrelated to voting procedures, campaign finance, or election administration.
No data-privacy, surveillance, or technology-regulation provisions exist.

Although federal employee compensation is tangentially related to labor policy, the bill addresses only the statutory COLA formula and does not alter collective-bargaining rights, union dues, or workplace rules.
The bill contains no religious-exemption or civil-rights language.
